outcome.Summary: Implemented `words.TopK` in words/words.go: it streams the reader in 1 MiB chunks through a rune-level state machine (words = maximal runs of Unicode letters/digits; an apostrophe joins a word only when flanked by letters, leading/trailing ones are stripped; words are lower-cased and stop words filtered case-insensitively), then returns the k most frequent words ordered by count descending with byte-order ascending tie-break (k<=0 returns an empty non-nil slice, read errors are returned). Memory stays bounded (one buffer + distinct-word map) and UTF-8 sequences split across chunk boundaries are handled via a copied tail buffer — I fixed a buffer-aliasing bug found through a byte-at-a-time test. Verified with words/words_test.go covering basic counting, case folding, stop words, apostrophe forms, Unicode/digits, tie ordering, k edge cases, read errors, a 64 KB single-line stream, and a 200-trial random property test against an independent oracle tokenizer; `go vet` and `go test ./...` both pass (exit 0).
